comment: Blocks for the patch designer. A chain of these becomes one SynthDef.
The chain reads the instrument's own output from the main pair, passes it
through each block in order, and ReplaceOuts the result -- the placement
makeup.py already proved on this machine. Moog's five effect slots are never
touched and no LADSPA node is ever freed; see engine.go for why that matters.
Every UGen here is registered by one of the 96 plugin .so scsynth loads at
boot. Input ORDER was read off sclang's own compiled output rather than
recalled -- LPF(in, freq), RLPF(in, freq, rq), CombC(in, maxdelay, delay,
decay), Limiter(in, level, dur) -- because a wrong argument order is a patch
that sounds wrong rather than a patch that errors.
A mono block is instantiated once per channel. A stereo block sees both.
Every block's parameters become SynthDef controls, so a slider can move them
on a running patch instead of rebuilding it.

blocks.title: Gain
blocks.blurb: Level, before everything after it. The output is limited whatever this says.

blocks.title: Low-pass
blocks.blurb: A gentle 12 dB slope. Takes the top off without resonance.

blocks.title: High-pass
blocks.blurb: Removes rumble and DC. Useful before a reverb.

blocks.title: Resonant low-pass
blocks.blurb: With resonance. rq is the inverse of Q -- smaller is more resonant.

blocks.title: Delay
blocks.blurb: A comb delay with feedback. Long decay times build up -- watch the meter.

blocks.title: FreeVerb2
blocks.blurb: A stereo Schroeder reverb, resident on your instrument since it shipped and unreachable from it. Size 0.8 is a 2.4 second tail, measured.

blocks.title: GVerb
blocks.blurb: A big physical-room reverb. Mono in, so the pair is summed before it. Costly -- the meter and the headroom number are there for this.

blocks.title: Tremolo
blocks.blurb: Amplitude modulation. The LFO runs at control rate, which costs almost nothing.
